modern: It is not right to be angry with things, For they do not care about it at all.
original: It is not right to vex ourselves at things, For they care nought about it.

explained.summary:
Here begins a run of quotations Marcus has collected, mostly lines from Greek plays. This one, from Euripides: there’s no point being angry with things, because they don’t care at all.

He keeps it because it neatly states a Stoic point: events and objects are indifferent to your fury, so anger at them only hurts you.
explained.today: Swearing at a printer that jams, kicking a flat tyre or glaring at the rain changes nothing in the world. It only changes your mood for the worse.
